body:
## Problem

`an land` reports a stack as ready and starts merging even when trunk has moved on and a later branch in the stack no longer replays cleanly onto it. The conflict only shows up after the first merge, during survivor maintenance, so the landing stops halfway: one PR is merged, the rest are not, and the user has to resolve the conflict in a half-landed state.

Observed with Anthracite `0.9.x` (`0.9.2` installed at the time of writing) on macOS (zsh).

## Observed setup and command

A stack of three PRs on `main`: `A` → `B` → `C`. While the stack was in review, an unrelated PR that touched the same files as `B` was merged into `main` on GitHub. Locally, `main` had not been fetched since.

```sh
an land C
```

The preview noticed that `main` had moved, but still reported the plan as ready:

```text
Target: C -> main
Policy: 1 required approval(s); required checks: none
Local main: fast-forward required.

🔀 PR order (bottom to top):
  Merge 1: A #95
  Merge 2: B #102 (publication deferred until its merge preparation)
  Merge 3: C #103 (publication deferred until its merge preparation)
...
✅ Readiness: READY for next merge only; later targets require publication and fresh checks.
✔ Apply this landing plan? … yes
✅ Confirmed merged #95.
ERROR: Landing incomplete at survivor maintenance. Confirmed merged #95 (9518299…); later work unattempted. Local replay conflict in B. Resolve and stage files, run an continue in <repo>, then rerun an land C --yes for remote maintenance.
```

`B` conflicted with the PR that had landed on `main` in the meantime, in 8 files. Resolving it took a real merge of two features, done in the middle of a landing with `A` already on `main`.

A first attempt a few minutes earlier had stopped with `Landing scope/readiness changed after confirmation; preview again. No changes made.`, possibly because an optional check finished or `main` moved between the preview and the confirmation. That one did no harm; the second one did.

## Expected behavior

When trunk has moved past the base of the stack, the preview checks whether every branch to be landed, and every surviving descendant, still replays onto the new trunk, before the first merge:

1. Try the replay without changing anything, for example with `git merge-tree` or in a temporary worktree.
2. If a branch conflicts, report the plan as NOT READY, naming the branch and the conflicting files, and suggest syncing or restacking first (`an sync`, or `an restack` after a fetch).
3. Only start the first merge when the whole chain replays cleanly.

That way the conflict is resolved while nothing is merged yet, the PRs are pushed with the resolved code so CI and reviewers see what will actually land, and READY means ready.

Running a full `an sync` automatically is probably too much, since it also touches other stacks; a read-only replay check is enough to refuse the landing early.

## Workaround

Run `an sync` (or fetch and `an restack`) before `an land`, resolve any conflicts, push, and only then land.
title: Check that the stack replays onto a moved trunk before land starts merging
